observations.text: SP, due to a briefing method that treated CRM as a separate topic instead of integrating it into the mission briefing, did not cover the CRM items of mission planning, communication and airmanship for the planned maneuvers. Throughout the flight the division of duties between the cockpits was left unstated and the SP could not work the practice emergency without assistance, with the result that the IP directed the sequence of actions and executed part of it. The CRM box was checked only after the IP built the debriefing points on the SP's behalf.

SP, due to inadequate crew coordination between front and rear cockpit, did not use the CRM concept when analyzing the simulated emergency and left the aircraft state unverbalized to the IP. The SP did not reach the required course of action without assistance, with the result that the IP allocated the roles and executed part of the procedure. During the debriefing the areas for CRM development were identified by the IP and not by the SP.

SP integrated CRM into the briefing and the debriefing at the level expected for the training section; however, the IFG/CRM matrix chart was used to highlight the particular items only after the IP's verbal prompts, on two occasions. Communication of the aircraft state to the front cockpit was passed with delay each time it was required. Marginal performance for the training section - independent use of the CRM matrix chart, without prompting, is expected to improve.

SP integrated CRM into the briefing and the debriefing without the IP's prompting, using the IFG/CRM matrix chart to highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items. Minor omissions in verbalizing the aircraft state during the working phase were recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention. The CRM concept was used when planning the maneuvers and the debriefing points were raised by the SP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP applied the CRM concept accurately and without delay in the briefing, throughout the flight and in the debriefing, and used the IFG/CRM matrix chart to highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items. The division of duties between the cockpits was stated before each maneuver and every deviation from the briefed plan was communicated as it was recognized, without the IP's intervention. The areas for CRM development were raised on the SP's own initiative during the debriefing. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated CRM performance above the desired level for the training section, integrating the CRM items into the briefing and the debriefing in a standardized manner and using the IFG/CRM matrix chart without any prompting. When the practice emergency was introduced, the SP stated the role allocation, requested the information needed from the front cockpit in plain language and analyzed the situation through the CRM concept before selecting the course of action. Coordination deviations across the sortie were negligible, and in the debriefing the SP set the areas for CRM development and solicited comments on where CRM enhanced mission effectiveness and flight safety. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to mission planning carried out without any CRM structure, did not brief the division of duties, the communication plan or the airmanship items for the planned profile. Throughout the flight the intentions of the two cockpits were never consolidated and the SP did not complete the sequence without assistance, with the result that the IP directed the entry to each maneuver and executed part of the recovery. The CRM box was checked only after the IP conducted the debriefing points on the SP's behalf.

SP, due to the authority gradient in the IP/SP cockpit, which suppressed an upward challenge, did not communicate a recognized deviation from the briefed profile and did not state "unable" when the sequence could no longer be flown as planned. The situation was not analyzed through the CRM concept and the SP did not complete the maneuver without assistance, with the result that the IP directed the correction and took the aircraft for part of the recovery. In the debriefing the SP identified the communication breakdown only after the IP pointed it out.

SP, due to a briefing flow that omitted the IFG/CRM matrix chart, did not highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items applicable to the sortie. Throughout the flight the aircraft state and the intended next action were passed to the front cockpit only after the IP asked for them, on three occasions. The required CRM calls were made with delay and the debriefing points were raised only after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP, due to workload management that left the checklist unfinished before the descent, did not maintain the communication element of CRM while flying the recovery. The intentions of the two cockpits were consolidated only after the IP prompted verbally for a position and fuel state report. Recognition of the coordination lapse came with delay, and the areas for CRM improvement were reached in the debriefing only under the IP's guidance.

SP integrated the CRM items into the briefing, the flight and the debriefing within the standards of the training section; however, communication of the aircraft state twice lagged the actual configuration change before the SP corrected it without the IP's intervention. The IFG/CRM matrix chart was used, but the airmanship subcategories were highlighted in less depth than the mission planning and communication items. Marginal performance for the training section - consistency in verbalizing the aircraft state at the moment of the change is expected to improve.

SP applied the CRM concept accurately and without delay when planning the maneuvers and when analyzing the simulated emergency, using the IFG/CRM matrix chart to highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items. Role assignment between the cockpits was stated before each maneuver and every configuration change was verbalized without the IP's intervention. In the debriefing the SP identified the point at which CRM enhanced mission effectiveness and flight safety and proposed the areas for CRM development. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated CRM performance above the desired level for the training section, integrating the CRM items into the briefing and the debriefing in a standardized manner and using the IFG/CRM matrix chart without prompting. Under the increased workload of the practice emergency the SP assigned the roles explicitly, requested the required information from the front cockpit in plain language and worked the problem as a crew rather than individually. Coordination deviations across the sortie were negligible and in the debriefing the SP solicited comments on where CRM enhanced mission effectiveness and flight safety. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a mission planning phase conducted without the CRM structure required for the profile, did not brief the division of duties, the communication plan or the airmanship items. Throughout the flight the two cockpits worked from different assumptions about the next maneuver and the SP did not complete the sequence without assistance. The IP directed the entry and executed part of the recovery, and the debriefing points were built by the IP and not by the SP.

SP, due to an unclear handover of aircraft control between IP and SP, did not confirm who was flying and who was working the procedure when the abnormal indication was introduced. The situation was not analyzed through the CRM concept, inputs were made from both cockpits at the same time and the SP did not complete the procedure without assistance. The IP resolved the ambiguity and executed part of the actions, and the CRM box was checked only after the IP led the debriefing.

SP, due to a debriefing method that reviewed the maneuvers without reference to the IFG/CRM matrix chart, did not highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items of the sortie. Throughout the flight the required CRM calls were passed only after the IP's verbal prompts and the coordination lapse was recognized with delay. The areas for CRM development were reached only after the IP directed the discussion toward them.

SP, due to absent inquiry when the observed aircraft performance did not match the expected, did not question the shared plan with the front cockpit and did not use the CRM concept while analyzing the developing situation. The discrepancy was raised only after the IP prompted verbally and the plan was corrected with delay. In the debriefing the SP described the communication breakdown only once the IP had structured the point.

SP, due to a briefing sequence that covered the communication plan after the maneuver descriptions instead of together with them, did not tie the required calls to the specific points of the profile. During the working phase two calls were passed late relative to the briefed points, and the SP recognized the mismatch and re-established the briefed communication flow without the IP's intervention. The CRM items were reviewed in the debriefing using the IFG/CRM matrix chart.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with navigation, communication and aircraft control attempted simultaneously, did not verbalize the aircraft state to the front cockpit at the configuration change. The omission was recognized by the SP shortly afterwards and the state was passed without the IP's intervention, so that the shared picture between the cockpits was restored. Minor coordination errors of this type occurred twice and were self-corrected in a timely manner.

SP applied the CRM concept in the briefing, throughout the flight and in the debriefing with the accuracy and the speed expected for the training section; however, the airmanship subcategories were highlighted on the IFG/CRM matrix chart only after a short pause on each occasion. Communication with the front cockpit was correct in content, with the transmission of the aircraft state at the configuration change made just inside the briefed timing. Marginal performance for the training section - a faster and more automatic use of the CRM matrix chart is expected to improve.

SP demonstrated CRM performance above the desired level for the training section, with the CRM items of mission planning, communication and airmanship integrated into the briefing and the debriefing in a standardized manner. Throughout the flight the role assignment was stated before every maneuver, the aircraft state was verbalized on each configuration change and the SP used the IFG/CRM matrix chart to close the points carried forward from the previous debriefing. Coordination deviations were negligible and the SP identified, without any prompting, the phase in which CRM enhanced mission effectiveness and flight safety. Above end of block MIF achieved.
